mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the federal funds rate is inversely related to S&P 500 forward returns due to increased discount rates on equity cash flows, as observed in historical data across multiple monetary policy cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS is above 5.0% (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 5 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% signals an overheating labor market that typically triggers central bank tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 3.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 5 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0% and the unemployment rate falls below 3.5%, the economy enters a late-cycle phase characterized by aggressive monetary tightening amid a tight labor market, which has historically led to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative in instances where FEDFUNDS > 5.0% and UNRATE < 3.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 5 years is below 0.03.
